Industry News: Visa Paid About $335 per Share to Buy Back $20.5 Billion of Its Stock Last Year. Would You Pay $400?

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (545 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 25, 2026 at 11:08AM EST.
  • In a recent development, it is often viewed as a good sign when companies buy back their own stock.
  • For the full fiscal year, Visa paid an average of roughly $335 per share for the stock it repurchased.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 25, 2026 at 11:08AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Visa ›.

In a recent development, it is often viewed as a good sign when companies buy back their own stock. So it is nice to see that Visa (V -0.05%) bought back $4 billion in shares in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 and $24.4 billion for the full fiscal year. However, note that the $4 billion is relatively small, suggesting the company wasn't as excited about its own stock in the final quarter of the year as it was earlier in the year. You'll probably be even less excited about it now that the shares are trading around $400. Here's why.

For the full fiscal year, Visa paid an average of roughly $335 per share for the stock it repurchased. In the fourth quarter, that price was $369. That helps explain why it bought less of the stock. In fact, the largest repurchase occurred in the second quarter of fiscal 2026, when the financial giant spent $7.9 billion at an average purchase price of roughly $320 per share. Very clearly, Visa bought less when the stock price was higher.

Recent findings suggest that with the stock currently trading around $400 per share, the organization's spending is likely to be even lower. And there's a good reason for that when you look at traditional valuation metrics. At the current share price, the stock's price-to-sales ratio is 18.4x, just a touch lower than its five-year average of 19.4x. The price-to-earnings ratio is roughly 32x, compared to a five-year average of 31x. And the price-to-book ratio is 21x versus a five-year average of nearly 15x. Given those valuation metrics, it is hard to suggest that the stock is cheap.

NYSE · As of 11:15 AM ET 11/25/26.

Industry observers note that visa may keep buying stock, since it is generating strong cash flows. Stock buybacks help support earnings by reducing the number of shares outstanding. And they allow the tech giant to return value to shareholders without committing to maintaining a larger dividend. As an investor buying the stock for your own portfolio, however, those aren't the types of concerns you are considering. You need to ensure that you pay an attractive price for a business you want to hold for the long term. As noted, after a rally, Visa's price no longer looks attractively cheap.

In a recent development, visa is a well-run company with long-term business appeal. It probably wouldn't be a huge mistake to buy it today, assuming you intend to hold it for the long term. However, the current price, which is well above the level at which Visa was making its most aggressive repurchases, doesn't look like a value opportunity. At best, you are paying full fare to own Visa right now, if not a premium.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By The Motley Fool Team – Nov 25, 2026 at 11:10AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than AdaptHealth ›.

In a recent development, on its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 3, 2026, AdaptHealth (AHCO -1.16%) raised its full-year guidance after stabilizing core operational performance. The home medical equipment provider is turning around its largest capitated contract--a fixed-payment agreement per patient regardless of service volume--while shedding non-core assets to pay down debt.

Three things management mentioned stand out.

According to recent reports, management cut headcount by more than 12% on its largest capitated agreement after surging patient demand drove losses earlier in the year. That cost discipline restored profitability to the contract and lifted adjusted EBITDA, or earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization.

In a recent development, A midyear contract termination and unexpected price increase from a equipment manufacturer threatened $30 million in second-half earnings. Management negotiated a new rebate structure to recover lost cash and established stable pricing terms for the upcoming contract year.

Industry observers note that the pending sale of the Diabetes Health segment allows AdaptHealth to eliminate non-core operations and direct sale proceeds toward lowering its $1.85 billion net debt burden. Exiting low-margin product lines leaves a streamlined business centered on continuous patient relationships in sleep and respiratory care.

In a recent development, third-quarter net revenue grew 10.9% year over year to $745.6 million, and operational recovery is taking hold across core segments. Exclusive provider agreements, digital patient tools, and a dedicated sales team provide lasting distribution advantages as leadership focuses on cost discipline.

Streamlining the product portfolio positions the firm to pay down debt and improve margins. Capital deployment remains tied directly to balance-sheet health.

#120314. Nvidia’s Jensen Huang Should Do This 1 Thing Now

📖 Baca
Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

Nvidia’s Jensen Huang Should Do This 1 Thing Now

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (821 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nvidia (NVDA -8.80%) today sits at the top of the artificial intelligence (AI) space.
  • This proved to be a game-changing move because AI took off -- and to power its use and development, the GPU became a crucial tool.
  • Nvidia may function like a well-oiled machine today.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adria Cimino – Nov 25, 2026 at 11:12AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

Nvidia (NVDA -8.80%) today sits at the top of the artificial intelligence (AI) space. The success story started about a decade ago: The tech giant entered AI early, well before the boom began, with an ambitious bet. Chief Jensen Huang saw the opportunity for Nvidia's graphics processing units (GPUs), once used mainly for gaming, to suit AI, and he shifted the company's focus to this area.

This proved to be a game-changing move because AI took off -- and to power its use and development, the GPU became a crucial tool. Though rivals have emerged, Nvidia holds onto the lead, as strong relationships with customers and its innovation have kept it ahead. All of this has resulted in spectacular earnings growth and stock price performance.

Nvidia may function like a well-oiled machine today. But something that happened recently revealed a significant flaw, and one that represents a risk over the long run. To address it, Huang should do one thing right now.

Jensen Huang. Image source: Getty Images.

Recent findings suggest that first, though, we'll take a quick look at Nvidia's position in the AI chip market and the recent event that brought attention to the risk I just mentioned. Nvidia's chips are the most powerful around, and with each new release, performance improves -- as a result, customers continue to rush to Nvidia for compute.

The tech giant recently stated that the ramp of its latest platform, Vera Rubin, was its fastest ever. That platform brought in nearly $20 billion in the third quarter, its first period of commercialization. And the firm's total revenue soared more than 100% to $115 billion, while net income also climbed in the triple digits to $65 billion.

It has been revealed that news regarding Nvidia has generally been positive throughout the AI boom, but earlier this month, one particular thing interrupted this cadence. Huang stepped down from his position as chief executive officer. This followed allegations of affairs -- one with a person that U.S. intelligence calls a Chinese spy and the other with an Nvidia executive. Without a succession blueprint, the board named current finance chief Colette Kress as interim CEO and began a search for a permanent replacement. Huang returned 11 days later following a massive wave of public support. The board decided to reinstate Huang after extensive interviews with him and input from senior U.S. government officials.

During Huang's absence, the stock fell 24%, and it soared more than 30% in the trading session following his return.

NASDAQ · As of 11:17 AM ET 11/25/26.

Now, here's the flaw I mentioned earlier: Nvidia doesn't have a succession plan. We recently got a glimpse of the impact of a Huang departure, as investors and analysts worried about the company's strategy moving forward without the visionary leader -- and this greatly affected stock performance. So, we could imagine that if Huang decided to retire or leave for any other reason, the same situation probably would unfold again.

Recent findings suggest that this is why the one thing Huang should do now is the following: name a successor and commit to moving into the chairman role by an age of his choice. The move would offer investors a certain level of comfort, knowing that one particular person has been named and shaped by Huang for the opportunity to lead Nvidia through its next chapters of growth. We've seen this done successfully at other companies, from Berkshire Hathaway to, just recently, Apple.

It has been revealed that announcing a succession plan would definitely be a positive move for Nvidia right now, particularly since we just witnessed the uncertainty brought on by Huang's absence. Will this happen, though? It seems unlikely. Upon his return, Huang told Nvidia staff that the company operates differently than others and therefore doesn't need a succession plan, CNBC reported, citing people at the meeting. He added that a plan would create unnecessary hierarchy, according to CNBC.

Huang, who has 60 direct reports, has mentioned that many strong leaders are in charge of various parts of the company. It's great to have many people involved, but investors still like to see one person in place to guide the general strategy. This one point of reference, a person investors can look to and trust, is essential. And without it, Nvidia stock may face periodic volatility -- particularly when investors think back to what unfolded in recent days.

Tokenization platform Securitize gains 10% postmarket on Q3 results, move into asset-backed finance

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (438 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tokenization platform Securitize climbed about 10% postmarket after reporting third quarter growth alongside increased operating expenses, and announcing an expansion into asset-backed finance through a strategic acquisition.
  • It has been revealed that miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively new corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure.
  • The growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tokenization platform Securitize climbed about 10% postmarket after reporting third quarter growth alongside increased operating expenses, and announcing an expansion into asset-backed finance through a strategic acquisition.

It has been revealed that miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively new corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure. Tokenized assets on the platform grew 9% in the third quarter, to $4.8 billion, from the same period a year ago. Aggregate transaction volume rose 20% from a year ago, to $4.3 billion. Revenue of $11.5 million was up 28% from last year.

The growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept. 17, which created a temporary pathway for trading of certain tokenized stocks and strengthened the regulatory outlook.

Profitability is still meaningfully below year-ago levels, due in part to costs associated with going public over the summer, as well as the scaling up of the tokenization business at an active time for the entire sector, Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo told CNBC in an exclusive interview.

Securitize reinforced "certain areas of the company like finance, compliance, legal [and] cybersecurity," which increased corporate costs "compared to a year ago when we were privately held," Domingo noted. "We're in in a very good position. The adjusted EBITDA … is improving significantly from previous quarters.".

Securitize reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of $2 million, compared with positive adjusted EBITDA of $3.6 million a year ago, better than a $5.5 million loss in the second quarter. The organization posted a 183% increase in operating costs and expenses.

Also on Monday, the Securitize board authorized a $50 million share buyback and announced the acquisition of River One, an institutional asset-backed financing platform developing technology to connect stablecoin capital with traditional lending markets. Terms were not disclosed.

Securitize sees an opportunity to modernize the $9 trillion market for asset backed finance by using stablecoins to finance real world assets, generate yield and tokenize investment positions and credit products, Domingo said.The acquisition also marks an expansion beyond Securitize's core niche markets at a time when tokenization's competitive landscape is growing, with traditional asset managers like BlackRock and Franklin Templeton, and established financial market infrastructure providers like DTCC and Broadridge, entering the industry.

"We have been very active in tokenized funds, treasuries [and] yield … And we've been obviously recently very active in tokenized stocks, so this adds another piece of the puzzle in the emerging tokenization space for us to capture revenue growth.".

Three things management noted stand out.

In a recent development, opening fresh housing developments expands total selling capacity without requiring new debt financing. Management expects its active community footprint to grow by roughly 20% over the next year.

Operational efficiency allows homebuilders to protect profits during uncertain economic cycles. Management reduced selling, general, and administrative expenses (SG&A)--the overhead required to run daily operations--in absolute dollars while top-line revenue grew.

Industry observers note that slashing home prices drives short-term order volume but damages core profitability. Management uses targeted incentives like mortgage rate buydowns to assist buyers, but it won't cut structural margins simply to boost sales counts.

Affordability pressures continue to test entry-level buyers, but management isn't backing away from its move-in ready spec home strategy (homes built before securing a buyer contract). Financial flexibility remains supported by an extended $1.2 billion revolving credit facility, a flexible credit line funding operations through October 2030, alongside lower balance sheet leverage. Management is watching buyer qualification timelines and absorption rates while maintaining strict pricing discipline across every market.

Expanding the active community base and controlling operational expenses keep the builder well positioned for multiyear value creation.

Billionaire Stanley Druckenmiller Sold 94% of His TSMC Stake and All of His Alphabet Shares in Q3. Here’s the Brilliant Stock He Added.

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that with the latest rounds of 13Fs out, investors get to see what billionaire hedge fund managers were up to in the third quarter.
  • Sources indicate that but should you follow his lead?
  • Druckenmiller hasn't allocated a large portion of his portfolio to AI-related stocks, and in Q3, he sold two prominent ones.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Keithen Drury – Nov 25, 2026 at 11:17AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Alphabet ›.

Sources indicate that with the latest rounds of 13Fs out, investors get to see what billionaire hedge fund managers were up to in the third quarter. One investor I follow is Stanley Druckenmiller, who runs the Duquesne Family Office. Druckenmiller has a strong history of picking great stocks, and he made some interesting moves in Q3.

Sources indicate that but should you follow his lead? Let's take a look at what he did.

Druckenmiller hasn't allocated a large portion of his portfolio to AI-related stocks, and in Q3, he sold two prominent ones. He fully exited his 336,300-share position in Alphabet (GOOG -4.94%) (GOOGL -5.32%), which is actually something he has done before. He held Alphabet shares in Q4 2025, then sold that position entirely in Q1 before buying the stock again in Q2. With Alphabet being one of the poster children for the AI build-out, this sale is notable.

Recent findings suggest that taiwan Semiconductor (TSM -7.12%) is another manufacturer often cited as one of the best AI investments, as it manufactures the lion’s share of the high-end chips that end up in nearly every AI computing unit. It has had tremendous returns over the past few years, and Druckenmiller has maintained a large position since Q4 of last year. However, he sold off around 94% of his TSMC holdings — his No. 2 position as of the end of Q2 — and he may close it fully in Q4 (if he hasn't bought any recently).

Those were two notable sales, but what did he buy instead?

Druckenmiller added a fair bit of Amazon (AMZN -5.88%) stock to his portfolio during Q3, bringing it from his ninth-largest position to his third-largest position. Amazon is still somewhat of an AI investment, as it gets a hefty chunk of its operating profit from its cloud computing division, Amazon Web Services (AWS). AWS has seen its growth rate boosted by rising cloud workloads, driven by increased AI usage.

NASDAQ · As of 11:11 AM ET 11/25/26.

According to recent reports, these were some interesting moves by Druckenmiller, but is that still the right strategy? I'd say no. These holdings were as of Sept. 30, and a lot has shifted in the market since then.

Since Q3 ended, Amazon has essentially been flat. Meanwhile, Alphabet has sold off by more than 20%, while Taiwan Semiconductor is down by 30%. Those were major declines, and Druckenmiller got out ahead of them, which suggests that he saw which way the wind would be blowing.

However, selling those stocks now could be a mistake because the prices are so much lower. In fact, Druckenmiller could be buying those two stocks back right now, but we won't know until Q4 data is released in mid-February.

With that in mind, I think investors should consider doing at this point the exact opposite of what the Duquesne Family Office did in Q3, as the landscape has shifted over the past month and a half.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal will host old nemesis José Mourinho’s Real Madrid in the league phase of the Champions League.

Mourinho, the former Chelsea, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur manager, will return to London to resume hostilities against last season’s beaten finalists.

Other reunions from Thursday’s draw include Manchester City travelling to Barcelona, to whom they last week sold Rodri, and Liverpool visiting Inter Milan, who have signed Curtis Jones.

Sources indicate that arsenal will also travel to Harry Kane’s Bayern Munich, while United will host the Germans as well on their Champions League return in a repeat of the legendary 1999 final. Michael Carrick’s side will also visit Cesc Fàbregas’s Como.

Mourinho last managed at the Emirates Stadium in March 2021, barely a month before his sacking by Spurs.

During his two spells as Chelsea manager, Mourinho famously had run-ins with Arsenal’s Arsène Wenger.

Mourinho called Wenger a “specialist in failure” after the Frenchman failed to add to his three Premier League titles following his Portuguese counterpart’s arrival in London in 2004.

Last season, Mikel Arteta finally ended Arsenal’s long wait to be crowned champions of England but agonisingly missed out on European glory.

Verdict Premier League champions should not be daunted by any game, but Real Madrid – with Mourinho in control – has the feel of a defining match of the group stage. Facing Kane in Munich does not seem any easier. Some tough assignments here including a trip to Napoli but the pot-four teams seem straightforward for Mikel Arteta.

Verdict Playing against the European champions and travelling to Barcelona will be a true test of how much progress Enzo Maresca has made in the short time he has been at the Etihad Stadium. City’s other games do not look easy either but they should be defeating teams such as Sporting Lisbon and Porto – at least they would be expected to under Pep Guardiola.

Industry observers note that verdict The San Siro was where Arne Slot began to turn results around last season and Iraola getting a win there would be a massive statement. Atlético staged a comeback at Anfield in 2020 and the repeat fixture will be tight. But there are enough winnable games there for Liverpool to reach the next round.

Recent findings suggest that verdict They will face a wall of noise in Istanbul when they play Galatasaray, but Villa will look to get points from the game. There are some tasty destinations for travelling fans and getting results there will ease the pressure on the match against PSG, who have been rattled by Villa before but remain a difficult opponent. The Nou Camp is a place where momentum can change in a season – for good or bad.

Verdict The repeat of the 1999 final is the standout fixture, but Michael Carrick should be looking beyond that match for the points needed to progress. He has been given a tough set of away games to navigate. They are winnable but difficult. So those games at Old Trafford will be very important.

Recent findings suggest that that brings our coverage of the Champions League draw to an end, as the 36 teams found which eight teams they will be facing in the league phase of this season’s tournament. Thanks for joining us!

The league phase will kick off on 8 September and will be wrapped up after all teams play at the same time on 27 January.

The top eight teams of the league phase progress to the last 16 automatically, while teams that finish between ninth and 24th will be forced to navigate a play-off tie to reach the knockout stages.

So we have 144 fixtures decided but there are certainly a few heavyweight contests which stand out:.

Sources indicate that that brings the draw to an end! Just a reminder that the order of the fixtures is based on the pots and the respective home and away fixtures within the pots, rather than chronology.

That is pots two and three done. Just the pot four teams to sort out now, finding out which other pot four teams they will face.

Some crackers in there. Up next we will be finding out all the opponents for the pot two teams.

Industry observers note that there is a fairly extensive video explanation of the format currently taking place. We should you be bringing you some fixtures very shortly...

The draw is now getting underway. Uefa deputy general secretary Giorgio Marchetti comes on stage to oversee proceedings. A reminder of the format:.

The 36 teams will be split into four pots of nine, based on “club coefficient rankings”, with defending champions Paris St-Germain automatically named as the top seed.

Proceedings will begin with a team from pot one being drawn at random, and they will be allocated eight fixtures – four at home and four away – by an automated software. They will face two teams from each pot, with one home game and one away game per pot, while they cannot play a team from their country.

This will be done for all nine teams from pot one, before the same process takes place for pot two teams, though they will already know their pot one opponents. Pot three teams will then find out their pot three and four opponents, before the pot four sides are allocated their fixtures against each other.

But before the draw we will be hearing from Villa about the 2011 final, which he scored in as Barcelona dismantled Manchester United at Wembley.

He calls it a “great generation” of players, mentioning Lionel Messi, who also scored in the 3-1 win.

Henry will be part of the draw so he remains on stage as Ceferin departs. David Villa will also be coming onto the stage to help with proceedings. We are told the draw will be starting shortly.

We’re hearing from Henry now about losing the 2006 Champions League final with Arsenal and winning three years later with Barcelona.

Recent findings suggest that he’s now discussing the current Arsenal crop and how they are getting closer to the trophy. He indicates if “they keep their core” and make some additions they can get over the line. But PSG “are an annoying team at the moment”.

Marquinhos on winning the respect award: “I’m very happy and honoured to be given this trophy. Fair play is an essential part of both football and daily life, and I will keep being respectful this year.”.

Recent findings suggest that up next is the “Uefa President’s Award”? The winner is of course Thierry Henry and, fortunately, he is in attendance, so he’s up on the stage to collect this honour. A slow clap from Martin Keown in the crowd.

Reshmin Chowdhury and Pedro Pinto shuffle the musicians off the stage before outlining this evening’s itinerary.

Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin is then brought up to the stage, after a quiet summer, to announce Marquinhos as the winner of a newly introduced award, the Respect Beyond the Game award.

Marquinhos is not at the ceremony, so it will be PSG president Nasser Al-Khelaifi coming up to collect it. We hear from the defender on a video message.

The ceremony is underway in Monaco with a live performance of the famous anthem – orchestra and all – while pictures of previous winners play on the big screen in the background.

All set for this evening's #UCL draw in Monaco 📌🏆 pic.twitter.com/N3verDUO9y.

Paris St-Germain will be aiming to become the first team to win three successive Champions Leagues since Real Madrid’s run of titles between 2016 and 2018.

The holders 🔴🔵#UCLdraw pic.twitter.com/eB05BNfWZi.

This season is the third under the new format, with a league phase instead of a group stage, and Uefa has confirmed that fixtures that have taken place in the league phase of the two previous seasons cannot be repeated this time around.

For example, Liverpool cannot host Real Madrid in the league phase this term after welcoming the 15-time European champions to Anfield at this stage of the previous two campaigns. Andoni Iraola’s side could, however, travel to the Bernabeu for an away meeting with Madrid.

Similarly, Arsenal will not be travelling to San Siro to face Inter, but could host the Serie A champions at the Emirates.

Arsenal finished top of the league phase last season after winning all eight fixtures and it resulted in a favourable run to the final, facing Bayer Leverkusen, Sporting and Atletico Madrid.

Liverpool, meanwhile, topped the league phase in the 2024-25 campaign – the first season with the new format – but fell at the first hurdle in the knockout stages after being drawn against Paris St-Germain.

The Ligue 1 side have proven that it’s not essential to be firing the whole way through the tournament, finishing 15th and 11th in the league phase in the last two seasons but going on to lift the trophy on both occasions.

Tom Gardner's Playbook for a Falling Stock Market

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (752 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that the S&P 500 (^GSPC -2.80%) fell about 3% in early trading Wednesday, and the Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC -4.24%) dropped more than 4% as chip stocks kept sliding.
  • It has been revealed that tom Gardner, The Motley Fool's co-founder and CEO, doesn't make market calls.
  • Put those together, and "a 10% to 15% decline in the S&P 500 should not be considered surprising or a remarkable development for any investor." His advice from that call reads even better now that the decline is here.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By The Premium Team – Nov 25, 2026 at 11:20AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›.

Sources indicate that the S&P 500 (^GSPC -2.80%) fell about 3% in early trading Wednesday, and the Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC -4.24%) dropped more than 4% as chip stocks kept sliding. It's the latest leg of a rough month. Last Friday, the S&P 500 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average both fell into correction territory, according to Charles Schwab (SCHW -1.81%).

It has been revealed that tom Gardner, The Motley Fool's co-founder and CEO, doesn't make market calls. What he gave members on the Fool's September Quarterly Call was closer to arithmetic. Stocks were trading 10% to 30% above their historical valuation ranges, he noted, and the S&P 500 has historically fallen 10% about once a year.

Put those together, and "a 10% to 15% decline in the S&P 500 should not be considered surprising or a remarkable development for any investor." His advice from that call reads even better now that the decline is here.

Industry observers note that tom warned that a drop wouldn't land evenly. When the S&P 500 falls 13%, he mentioned, "a lot of the high-growth, high-beta businesses around which our portfolios have grown actually get set back even more significantly.".

That's what happened last Friday, when the S&P 500 lost 3.7% and the Nasdaq fell 5.3%, and it's happening again today. If your account is down more than the index, that's the price of owning fast growers. Tom just wanted members to see the bill before it arrived.

His first recommendation was to lean toward "high-quality companies and lower expectations." He described investors who keep some cash on the side and use declines of 20% or 40% to buy more of their favorite companies at lower prices. That only works if the cash is there before the drop. Most people love a 30% sale at the mall and treat a 10% sale on stocks like a fire drill, and the difference usually comes down to whether they have money ready to spend.

Sources indicate that he also lowered the bar on returns. Tom noted he'd be happy with low-double-digit annual gains from here, and he wants investors to weigh not losing money as heavily as making it.

In a recent development, A day like today pushes people toward big moves. Selling everything feels like taking control, and so does pouring cash into a stock that just fell 15%. Tom thinks both impulses miss what conviction really looks like. He remarked "the best form of conviction is the step-by-step incremental moves," because buying or selling in stages makes you rethink your reasons each time.

Put another way, Tom says that "emotional reactivity is the enemy of wealth creation." He even expects more staged selling across certain holdings in Motley Fool portfolios to get members out of weak or aggressively valued positions sooner, since every trim forces a fresh look at the evidence.

His most useful idea had little to do with stocks. Tom suggested families figure out "how inexpensively can you live for a single month with a high enough quality of life?" Then use the answer to size an emergency fund of six, nine, or 12 months. Nobody's kids will beg to do it again, but the point, as he put it, is to "simulate a recession before it arrives." Once you know your bare-minimum monthly cost, you know how much cash to hold and how much money can sit through a downturn untouched.

Tom ended with something his father used to say after a long, happy day with the kids: "Tomorrow's another day." Investors who try to cram every gain into this year tend to burn out, and some quit the market for years.

Sources indicate that the market closes Thursday for Thanksgiving and reopens Friday for a short session. Before it does, figure out how many months of expenses your cash would cover. That number will say more about how the next year goes for you than anything the Nasdaq does on Friday.

As they scale, cash outflows for capital expenditures and manufacturing capacity expansion increase, while cash inflows are more uneven, causing free cash flow to fluctuate.

The Frenchman’s two goals included a captivating mazy dribble, which will long be remembered by those who had the fortune to see it.

Industry observers note that city created enough space for themselves through clever movement. With Cherki zigging one way and Phil Foden zagging the other, they created even more by dribbling past a mesmerised Palace back three that became a back five at times and still could not cope.

It has been revealed that erling Haaland also scored twice. Even with the creative and unpredictable talents of those behind in a four-man attacking City midfield, Haaland remains irreplaceable with his ability to convert chances.

In a recent development, however, this night belonged to Cherki. Guardiola chided him publicly after he set up a City goal with a “rabona” cross last season. The thrust of Guardiola’s comments were that Cherki was not Lionel Messi. Of course not, but he possesses a genius all of his own, which Maresca would surely be foolish to rein in.

The jaw-dropping splendour of Cherki’s first goal drew a collective intake of breath at Selhurst Park.

Collecting a Foden pass, he attacked the Palace area on a diagonal path, slaloming between Jaydee Canvot, Takehiro Tomiyasu and Chris Richards, before having the spatial awareness and technique to flick his left foot at the ball to send it rolling on a perpendicular trajectory past Dean Henderson.

"The man with the magic feet!"Rayan Cherki doubles Manchester City's lead with a STUNNING goal 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/9Zea5vFljv.

An insight into Cherki’s mindset came after the match.

He said: “My performance is s---. In the first half, we didn’t find the space, I played bad. I need to show them that I want to play, I want to score. Next time I want to give the ball around more.”.

Forget the words, Maresca cannot ignore the actions of a player he left on the bench against Bournemouth.

Sterner tests will come for City than against a Palace side missing key players who may or may not leave south London in the remaining days of the transfer window.

Whether Maresca will trust his forward players to express themselves as freely against their rivals for the Premier League title remains to be seen, but with Elliot Anderson providing a one-man shield behind them, City could not be stopped.

According to recent reports, maresca remarked: “For sure Rayan is happy tonight. His performance was very good and not just for his two goals. He has to press off the ball and he was in charge of [marking] Adam Wharton, so it was a complete game by him.”.

Only for the first three minutes did Palace hint at a different outcome but, after shots from Eddie Nketiah and Daichi Kamada were diverted away for corners, City took control.

They took the lead in the 17th minute when the otherwise quiet Antoine Semenyo flighted a cross over the heads of everyone except the shorn locks of Haaland, whose determined header looped over Henderson and dropped in the far corner.

The only negative of Foden’s performance came in front of goal, with a ballooned shot and a mistimed header.

After Cherki’s solo masterpiece had made it 2-0, Yeremy Pino seized the next moment for his own with a stunning free-kick that flicked the crossbar, then the back of City keeper Gianluigi Donnarumma before finally dropping over the line.

"This is a good a free-kick as you're likely to see this season!" Yéremy Pino's stirke beats Donnarumma 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5uF4vzOXDp.

Whatever hope that mustered was snatched away again when Cherki scored his second goal and the third goal of a breathless five minutes.

His shot at the end of a darting run flicked the ankle of Tomiyasu to send it just out of Henderson’s reach.

Rayan Cherki AGAIN! Manchester City have breathing room once again after another strike from the Frenchman 👏 pic.twitter.com/Tyw9whPS2r.

Morocco teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi had little time to show why City have paid Lille £85.6m for him with a late entry as a substitute, but they didn’t need him on this occasion.

Foden then set off on a swerving run that set up Haaland to lash home his second goal of the game and make it 4-1.

Erling Haaland scores gets another! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/4mz2eF7wFF.

The fear for Palace is that they cannot keep selling their best players and expecting to replicate the success on the pitch that has brought them three trophies in the past 15 months.

Leicester City offer a shuddering example of that. From Premier League champions to League One in 10 seasons.

Pierre Sage, the fresh Palace manager, will welcome the certainty that the closure of the transfer window will bring, particularly over the futures of forwards Ismaïla Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta, as well as wing-back Daniel Muñoz.

The one player he cannot afford to lose is Wharton, who matched the City midfield on his own at times in the first half.

Recent findings suggest that sage remarked: “I think the score is heavy. We stayed in the game for 65 minutes and created some chances. We know we are in for a tough season, but we have created a lot of opportunities in the first two games.

“I could speak about the transfer window, but I don’t want to find an excuse. We just have to be sure that in four days’ time, the team will be better than today.”.

Recent findings suggest that “It has been a short pre-season. Rayan [Cherki], five weeks ago was at the World Cup. Game by game, we will be back, just need a few games. We played well, it is a upcoming manager but we have been playing together, with the addition of a few new players. We know what to do and have to trust the system.”.

“We have to keep on playing together, find out where we are best and how to play. We have so many good players and we have to fit everyone in. He has to keep going because we know how good Phil is, it is about showing it week in week out. This is the right step forward for everyone. We have to build on this.”.

"I'm just trying to play my football" 💪Elliot Anderson is excited about the future at Manchester City after his summer transfer 🔥 pic.twitter.com/huGv4Li3GZ.

"Say what you actually mean!" 🤣Erling Haaland takes over Rayan Cherki's post-match interview! pic.twitter.com/adW6IU8DzQ.

It will take Pierre Sage a while to impose his style of play. It will certainly take another week before he knows his final squad for the first half of the season.

It was noticeable at the final whistle that many Palace fans stayed around to applaud Daniel Munoz, an unused substitute on the night, as he made his way to the tunnel, probably for the final time as a Palace player if Nottingham Forest’s interest in him becomes a transfer by the end of the window.

The first half at Selhurst Park is then brought to an end and Manchester City lead 1-0 at the break thanks to Haaland’s header.

There will be just one added minute at the end of this first half.

Palace started off with a nominal back three. That has become a back five far too often for Pierre Sage’s liking at times in this first half, yet still City are playing through them almost at will. The Palace fans whose deafening support accompanied Palace shots in the opening minutes are reduced to cheering battling midfield runs that win a free-kick now.

Semenyo’s shot from the left side of the box takes a deflection off Richards, forcing Henderson into a decent save.

Strand Larsen comes close with a header from a Pino cross but he would have been offside anyway.

Recent findings suggest that the first booking of the night goes the way of the visitors. Wharton drives forward into the Manchester City half and is cynically brought down by Cherki, who looked perplexed when the yellow card was shown but it was an obvious booking.

He waits for Cherki to make the overlapping run before passing to the Frenchman. Cherki’s cross picks out Foden inside the six-yard box and the latter should score but he gets a simple header all wrong.

Well, that was easy. So easy in fact – perfect Semenyo cross, perfect Haaland header - that it hushed Selhurst Park as the ball looped over Dean Henderson. Even the roar from the enclave of City fans took a moment to fill the south London air. You wouldn’t say that all the pre-match optimism among Palace fans has been punctured, but the home side need a moment if they aren’t to sink without trace to a City side bossing possession and territory now.

That is a huge miss from Foden. Anderson picks out his compatriot in acres of space on the right side of the box, with no Palace defender within five yards of him, but Foden blazes over the bar when he should have put Manchester City 2-0 up.

King Harald V of Norway has died in the last few days and over the last few hours two Norwegian cyclists claimed a one-two at the Vuelta a Espana and now Haaland has a goal.

Was it really just a year ago when Crystal Palace fans flooded down the Holmesdale Road with not a care in the world having just won the Community Shield to add to their FA Cup triumph over tonight’s opponents Manchester City? Well, they are marching along the Holmesdale Road in the same numbers again this evening, bedecked in red and blue as always, yet there is uncertainty and worry in the air and on their faces. Will the player exodus continue? What should they make of fresh manager Pierre Sage? Will the good times fade from view as rapidly as they did for Leicester City or can Sage build a new side to match the one which, under Oliver Glasner, added the Conference League to their list of trophies three months ago?

“We struggled to get into the game and win the battles,” a disappointed Carlo Ancelotti lamented.

In a recent development, at the World Cup, an industrious 18-year-old showed maturity beyond his years to dominate the midfield against Ancelotti’s Brazil on his competitive international debut, earning Morocco a draw. That was, in fact, the second time an Ancelotti side had been undone by precocious teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi.

It has been revealed that ancelotti’s remarks about losing the midfield battle are from after a Champions League match in October 2024, when Lille shocked Real Madrid to end their 36-game unbeaten run. Bouaddi was at the heart of both statement results for his club and country.

It has been revealed that the second weekend of the Premier League season kicks off under the lights in South London as Crystal Palace host Manchester City at Selhurst Park. Manchester City won both fixtures 3-0 last season and they are in fact unbeaten in their last 11 Premier league away games against Crystal Palace, who have won just two of the 22 top flight meetings.

Sources indicate that crystal Palace experienced defeat on the opening weekend, falling to a 2-0 loss at Everton last Saturday, meaning the Pierre Sage era started with a defeat. Tonight is Sage’s first home game in charge of the club.

“I think it will be a wonderful moment, but I prefer to have a wonderful moment with good news at the end of the game,” Sage remarked. “That is why I do not think about me in this situation. The most crucial thing is the team and the result for sure, because we prepare all the week for that, to make them [the fans] happy. They will be happy to see us, but I think they would prefer to see us win. I will give my life to make them happy. I cannot do more. When you are in this stadium [Selhurst Park], you feel the history. You feel that there is something heavy weighing on you. It is a great responsibility that I have been entrusted with. We cannot wait to see this stadium in action.”.

Recent findings suggest that sage has confirmed that Ismaila Sarr, who has been linked with a move away from the club this summer, and Chadi Riad will miss out tonight due to injury, as will striker Jean-Philippe Mateta. Palace have confirmed the addition of Axel Disasi on loan from Chelsea and the French defender could be involved tonight.

Sources indicate that manchester City appeared to be heading towards defeat in Enzo Maresca’s first league game in charge of the club last weekend. They were 1-0 down at home against Bournemouth in the closing stages before goals from Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol gave them a come-from-behind win.

Industry observers note that it has been a busy week in the transfer window for Manchester City. Both Savio (formerly Savinho) and Omar Marmoush have left for Tottenham, joining a long list of departures from the Etihad this summer. Moroccan midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi has arrived in an £85m deal from Lille and has become the most expensive teenager in Premier League history. Maresca has confirmed that 18-year-old Bouaddi is ready to start.

It has been revealed that “He [Bouaddi] is ready,” Maresca noted. “He was working with his former club so he is fit. We will see how long he needs in terms of adaptation but he is ready to go. He is quite calm. He does not look 18, he already looks older, which is important. But in this case, we need to go slowly because he is very young, he has come from a different country so there is no rush for him. He is going to help us now and in the future. He is very mature for being 18.”.

By The Premium Team – Nov 25, 2026 at 11:30AM EST.

If your stocks feel far jumpier than the market lately, you're not imagining it.

This past Friday, Nov. 20, Wall Street's best-known fear gauge, the VIX, closed at 35.89. That's high, but it's nowhere near a record. A lesser-known gauge that tracks the stocks inside the S&P 500 (^GSPC -2.80%) told a different story. It closed at 57.91, well above its long-run average of about 32.

On this month's Epic Opportunities podcast, Team Hidden Gems' Tyler Crowe called that gap "off the charts." Then he explained why it's happening.

In a recent development, the VIX tracks expected swings in the S&P 500 as a whole. The second gauge, the CBOE S&P 500 Constituent Volatility Index, or VIXEQ, does the same for the individual stocks in the index.

It has been revealed that single stocks always swing more than the index, so the VIXEQ normally sits above the VIX. But stocks are also moving out of step with each other far more than usual. When one soars and another sinks, those moves cancel out. So the index looks calmer than the stocks inside it.

Recent findings suggest that you've probably seen this in your own portfolio. Tyler pointed out that stocks are jumping 10% to 15% on a single earnings report. And on Monday, Nvidia (NVDA -8.63%), a firm worth trillions of dollars, "moved 30%" in a single day, as Tyler put it. "These things don't happen a lot," he stated.

Tyler pointed to three forces that, together, make big moves in individual stocks more likely.

It has been revealed that put them together, Tyler said, and you get amplified trades in a shrinking pool of shares. The result is massive daily moves, even in the world's largest companies.

Recent findings suggest that massive daily moves can feel alarming. But a 15% drop after an earnings report, or a 30% jump on a headline, may say more about how stocks trade today than about the business behind them.

It has been revealed that that's one reason we suggest owning 50 or more stocks. With a broad mix, many of those swings cancel each other out in your portfolio, just as they do in the index. Keeping each position to a sensible size helps too.

And when a stock you own makes a substantial move, ask one question before you act: Has anything changed in the business itself, or just the share price?

#120286. Industry News: What's ahead for AI financing after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang departs

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (745 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: What's ahead for AI financing after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang departs

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (745 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure hasn't produced a broad shock to the credit market, but it is putting the company's role as a financier of artificial intelligence infrastructure under scrutiny.
  • Huang, who stepped down Thursday amid an espionage and adultery scandal, built Nvidia into an AI powerhouse in the 33 years since he co-founded the manufacturer.
  • Nvidia not only supplies its graphics processing units to hyperscalers and tech giants, it also provides financing to other companies to help the industry expand.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure hasn't produced a broad shock to the credit market, but it is putting the company's role as a financier of artificial intelligence infrastructure under scrutiny.

Huang, who stepped down Thursday amid an espionage and adultery scandal, built Nvidia into an AI powerhouse in the 33 years since he co-founded the manufacturer. Chief financial officer Colette Kress has been named interim CEO as the company searches for a permanent chief executive.

Nvidia not only supplies its graphics processing units to hyperscalers and tech giants, it also provides financing to other companies to help the industry expand. That could all change.

"Although we expect the company to fulfill all of its previously unveiled commitments, we believe that going forward, it may be more difficult for the company to negotiate fresh multi-party investments among ecosystem partners at the same scale it has done up to this point," Goldman Sachs analyst James Schneider stated in a note Thursday.

The news of Huang's resignation comes after investors were already concerned about the massive amount of debt being taken on to fund AI infrastructure.

Recent findings suggest that tech bond yields have risen and spreads have widened on credit default swaps, most notably in lower-rated names. Credit default swaps are contracts in which investors pay for protection in case the borrower can't repay its debt. Wider spreads indicate investors view the bonds as riskier.

Sources indicate that on Friday, the yield on Nvidia's 4.5% bond due in 2031 sat at 5.717%, nearly 5% higher week to date. Bond yields move inversely to prices.

Sources indicate that tech stocks slumped Friday with the Nasdaq 100 closing down 1.2% as markets continued to digest the Nvidia news. Yields on hyperscaler bonds ticked slightly higher on Friday, signaling the broader concern about AI debt lingers.

Industry observers note that it's the smaller AI companies that could ultimately see an impact if Nvidia makes any changes to its AI financing. The organization had $36 billion in off-balance-sheet AI cloud agreements, or backstops, for neoclouds, according to its last quarterly financial filing in July.

Neoclouds CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN are all in Nvidia's portfolio. Their shares were down sharply Thursday.

CoreWeave, which has become the poster child for AI debt fears, saw its bond yields retreat after its quarterly earnings on Tuesday eased investor concerns. The yield on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 was 14.79% on Friday after climbing to 16.7% last week. The spread on its five-year CDS also dropped more than 17% week to date, although it remained above 1,000 — which is generally considered a sign of distress.

It remains unclear how Nvidia's support for those companies may change, noted CreditSights analyst Andy Li.

"We don't know what the ultimate strategy for Nvidia is going to be coming out the other side," he said.

"However, I think directionally, just given the fact that Jensen was so crucial in selling the Nvidia story and being a very aggressive deal maker, it's likely that a lot of this creative deal-making and circular financing and equity and credit support is going to moderate," he added.

CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator told CNBC Wednesday, before Huang's departure, that Nvidia "is not one person.".

"There are thousands of people over there that interface with thousands of people at my firm every day. They integrate on the technology. They integrate on the physical infrastructure. They integrate on the networking," he said in an interview with "Squawk on the Street." "They have been a great partner for us for years. They will continue to be a great partner for us.".

Industry observers note that bob Lang, founder and chief strategist at Explosive Options, doesn't see any big changes in terms of Nvidia's relevance or its ability to finance for now. As CFO, Kress was involved in the financing deals, and the search for a permanent CEO is going to take some time, he noted.

The real problem is just how much money the tech giant will want to lend for AI financing, rather than, say using its hundreds of billions in free cash flow for other purposes, like share buybacks, capex, or acquisitions.

Industry observers note that "Big companies like Nvidia and Meta, they're holding all the cards," he said. "When they decide that the game is over, that's it — it's going to be curtains for some of these smaller companies.".

— CNBC'S Kif Leswing and Isabel O'Brien contributed reporting.

Broadcom vs. Qualcomm: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Brendan Coffey – Updated Nov 25, 2026 at 11:32AM EST.
  • According to recent reports, as the race for dominance in infrastructure and wireless connectivity heats up, two semiconductor titans are vying for capital.
  • In a recent development, broadcom has pivoted heavily toward artificial intelligence and enterprise software, while Qualcomm remains the heavyweight champion of mobile handset technology.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Brendan Coffey – Updated Nov 25, 2026 at 11:32AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Broadcom ›.

According to recent reports, as the race for dominance in infrastructure and wireless connectivity heats up, two semiconductor titans are vying for capital. Investors must decide between Broadcom (AVGO -6.24%) and Qualcomm (QCOM -4.71%) for the long term.

In a recent development, broadcom has pivoted heavily toward artificial intelligence and enterprise software, while Qualcomm remains the heavyweight champion of mobile handset technology. They represent two different paths through the technology landscape, one focused on the data center and the other on the palm of your hand.

Broadcom operates as a leader in semiconductor stocks, providing essential components for data centers and networking. It maintains long-standing relationships with hyperscalers and companies with AI frontier models. Notable recent deals include a $200 billion memorandum of understanding with Samsung and a $30 billion chip commitment with Apple Inc. (AAPL -2.07%). Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business, as aggregate sales to the top five end customers account for approximately 40% of its total net revenue.

According to recent reports, in the 12 months ended Aug. 2, 2026, revenue reached about $89.1 billion, representing an increase of approximately 48.7% compared to the previous year. This substantial growth follows the manufacturer's strategic move to integrate high-value software assets alongside its hardware offerings. Net income for the same period was approximately $38.3 billion, reflecting a strong bottom line as the company capitalizes on the rising demand for AI-optimized infrastructure.

According to recent reports, as of its November 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 0.8x. This metric, which measures total debt against shareholder equity, suggests a moderate level of leverage. The current ratio, which compares current assets to current liabilities, is roughly 1.7x. In the fiscal year ended Nov. 2, 2025, free cash flow reached about $26.9 billion. Note that stock-based compensation (SBC) represented roughly 27.5% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

According to recent reports, qualcomm focuses on foundational wireless and computing technologies, primarily for handsets, automotive, and Internet of Things (IoT) markets. It derives a significant portion of its revenues from major mobile customers, including Apple and Xiaomi (XIACF -0.48%). While it is a leader in mobile modems, the company is actively expanding into automotive and data center solutions to diversify its reach. It also maintains a robust licensing business, working with hundreds of companies globally through its cellular patent portfolio.

In a recent development, in the 12 months ended Sept. 27, 2026, revenue was roughly $43.1 billion, which reflects a decrease of nearly 2.6% over the prior twelve-month period. This slight decline occurred as the company navigated a shifting mobile market and transitioned its focus toward new growth areas. Despite the revenue dip, the company reported net income of approximately $13.6 billion for the same period, showing its ability to maintain significant profitability in its core licensing and chip segments.

As of its September 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is roughly 0.5x. This figure indicates the relationship between total debt and shareholder equity. The current ratio is approximately 1.9x, indicating the manufacturer's ability to cover short-term obligations with current assets. In the fiscal year ended Sept. 27, 2026, free cash flow was close to $8.7 billion. Note that stock-based compensation accounted for roughly 31% of operating cash flow, inflating reported cash generation, since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

Broadcom faces risks from high customer concentration, as a small number of end customers and distributors account for a significant portion of its revenue. The company is also navigating intense competition and rapid technological change in the AI sector, which creates pricing pressure as standards evolve. Operations depend heavily on a limited number of contract manufacturers, specifically Taiwan Semiconductor, for wafer production. Furthermore, Broadcom manages legal and operational risks tied to its acquisition of VMware, including complex integration and tax liabilities.

Recent findings suggest that qualcomm deals with significant revenue concentration from a few mobile handset customers, making the loss of a single partner like Apple particularly impactful. Geopolitical tensions between the U.S. and China pose a threat to sales and supply chain stability in that region. Strategic expansion into automotive and data center markets brings Qualcomm into competition with established players like Marvell Technology (MRVL -9.25%). Additionally, the company faces ongoing legal and regulatory scrutiny regarding its patent licensing practices and antitrust investigations.

Qualcomm appears cheaper based on its significantly lower P/S ratio, although both companies trade at very similar Forward P/E levels based on future earnings estimates.

Valuation metrics include those sourced from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from those of other data providers.

Industry observers note that broadcom is seeing tremendous top-line momentum, with management projecting that fiscal 2026 will bring in about $115 billion in sales, almost double 2025's, and that the following year, fiscal 2027, will see revenue double 2026's to $230 billion. Net income in 2026 will be just about double 2025, at $45 billion, with profit of about $79 billion in 2027.

Sources indicate that the strength is coming from AI, with its six main hyperscale customers all increasing their long-term orders for chips and other equipment from Broadcom. These six hyperscalers include Alphabet Inc. (GOOG -4.94%), Meta Platforms (META -2.29%), Anthropic (ANT -3.34%), OpenAI and two firms whose names are not disclosed.

In a recent development, there is some risk to all this growth: one is that the AI boom could go bust, but probably more significant is that Broadcom and private equity giant Blackstone (BX -3.43%) have a joint financing venture that finances frontier AI labs to buy Broadcom equipment. The failure of a client to repay the loan or shifts in interest rates could cause problems with the finance arm and the business at large.

According to recent reports, meanwhile, Qualcomm's mobile phone business has been hammered this year, as weak Chinese demand and AI-driven memory shortages have caused handset-derived sales to fall below prior-year levels. Yet the AI boom has an upside for Qualcomm.

At the company's June 2026 investor day, Qualcomm raised its non-handset revenue target to more than $40 billion by 2029, nearly double the prior target of $22 billion. Qualcomm is reportedly partnering with OpenAI to develop smartphone processors with advanced AI capabilities. Analysts see this partnership as a positive for Qualcomm since it would enable advanced agentic AI on smartphone platforms. It would also diminish the business risk of Apple developing its own chips and dropping Qualcomm as a supplier.

Qualcomm may seem more attractive with its lower P/S ratio compared to Broadcom, but it seems too speculative right now on AI phone prospects, especially as its core mobile phone business is facing strong headwinds. Broadcom's growth and AI exposure are too good to ignore, and its forward P/E ratio of 15.8x is just slightly more than Qualcomm's and below the average forward P/E of the S&P 500. For 2027, Broadcom is the better buy.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Neil Patel – Nov 25, 2026 at 11:33AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Bitcoin ›.

November hasn't been kind to Bitcoin (BTC -1.43%). The most valuable cryptocurrency has tanked 21% this month (as of Nov. 24). It's presently trading below $60,000, near its lowest level in the past 12 months.

Sources indicate that bearish sentiment is clearly taking over. It's impossible to pinpoint an exact reason for the recent decline. A higher-for-longer interest rate environment amid ongoing above-average inflation might be nudging investors to take some risk off the table.

As a result, Bitcoin dominance, which measures the market capitalization of the top digital asset relative to the overall cryptocurrency industry, is 58.6%. Does this reading suggest that altcoins are ready to explode?

According to recent reports, bitcoin dominance is calculated by dividing its market cap by the total market cap of all cryptocurrencies. As the number rises, investors are sticking with the most established digital asset. When it falls, they're usually more interested in smaller and riskier coins.

That makes it a useful sentiment gauge for the entire crypto industry.

According to recent reports, history explains the excitement around a sub-60% reading. Bitcoin dominance started 2021 over 70% and sank to 40% by May. Altcoins like Dogecoin (SHIB -2.76%) and Shiba Inu (DOGE -2.08%) went wild that year. The same dynamic occurred to altcoins in 2017, when dominance plunged to an all-time low of about 37% in January 2018.

But those booms ended badly, and the most recent one is a warning. Dominance slipped below 60% in August 2025. It took two weeks for Ethereum (ETH -1.47%) to set a record of $4,953.73. Today, it trades under $1,700. That's a 66% plunge, worse than Bitcoin's 52% drop from its peak.

According to recent reports, this time, the setup looks different. Past declines in Bitcoin dominance were driven by greed, especially in 2021. Today's decline is driven by fear.

Industry observers note that stablecoins, which are digital tokens pegged to the U.S. dollar, provide insight. They're now worth about $281 billion. The market share of Tether (USDT -0.01%), the largest stablecoin, expanded by one percentage point this month to 62.1%. However, total stablecoin supply shrank by $13.6 billion in November, so they aren't attracting fresh cash.

It has been revealed that and investors aren't rotating into altcoins. The Altcoin Season Index sits at 57, far below the 75 that signals a true altcoin season.

CRYPTO · As of 11:22 AM ET 11/25/26.

Sources indicate that I don't think Bitcoin dominance offers a clear takeaway. Investors are better off focusing on the bigger picture.

Industry observers note that the rest of 2026 could stay rough. U.S. spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) saw $4.7 billion in net outflows this month. Nobody can predict when the selling will stop.

Sources indicate that but zoom out. Bitcoin's supply is capped at 21 million coins, and it operates with a predictable inflation rate. The next halving, which halves newly introduced supply from miners, is expected in April 2028. Scarcity is central to the thesis, and it's built into the code.

Wall Street has also entered the space. The three largest U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs held 1.1 million coins. According to River, a Bitcoin financial services firm, 16 leading U.S. banks have launched or are working on Bitcoin solutions for their customers. Bank of America (BAC -1.87%) lets its more than 15,000 wealth advisors recommend a 1% to 4% crypto allocation. Vanguard reversed course and opened its platform to crypto ETFs.

Bitcoin is the safest bet in the industry. It has the longest track record, the highest value, and the most institutional support. But safest doesn't mean it's free of risk or volatility. Despite being the oldest cryptocurrency with brand recognition, tremendous liquidity, and a global network effect, Bitcoin still experiences significant drawdowns.

According to recent reports, investors should size any position accordingly. And stay focused on the next decade, not the dominance chart.

    #120270. Ahead of Micah Parsons' return for Packers-Rams, Aaron Donald jokes: 'Micah, if you want to take one more week …'

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1749 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Yahoo ↗ Open Full Page

    Ahead of Micah Parsons' return for Packers-Rams, Aaron Donald jokes: 'Micah, if you want to take one more week …'

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1749 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Three-time Defensive Player of the Year Aaron Donald said what the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams might all be thinking: "I wish he would stay out one more week.".
    • Industry observers note that donald was referring to Packers edge rusher Micah Parsons.
    • Instead, the NFL's first Thanksgiving Eve game will feature a matchup of two teams who spent big to upgrade their pass rush recently — before injuries sunk their hopes within months.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Three-time Defensive Player of the Year Aaron Donald said what the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams might all be thinking: "I wish he would stay out one more week.".

    Industry observers note that donald was referring to Packers edge rusher Micah Parsons. A member of the Packers might also have applied the sentiment to Rams edge rusher Myles Garrett.

    Instead, the NFL's first Thanksgiving Eve game will feature a matchup of two teams who spent big to upgrade their pass rush recently — before injuries sunk their hopes within months.

    The Packers dealt their 2026 and 2027 first-round picks as well as defensive tackle Kenny Clark to the Dallas Cowboys in August 2025 in exchange for Parsons. He raced to 12.5 sacks last year as the Packers were 9-3-1 before Parsons tore his ACL and meniscus last Dec. 14.

    After 11 months, the Packers activated him this week with the expectation he'll debut Wednesday in first-year defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon's defense.

    Allow Donald, who emerged from a two-year retirement Aug. 30 to rejoin the Rams, to wish that Parsons would wait another week.

    It has been revealed that "A fan of Micah, I think he's one hell of a football player, fast, explosive, plays with an unbelievable motor," Donald told reporters on Sunday. "If he does play this week, that's going to be huge for them. Micah, if you want to take one more week to get yourself 100%, make sure everything is where it needs to be, I'd like to see you on TV.

    "I know they're going to be happy to have him back.".

    To the Packers' dismay, Garrett is back in the mix as well.

    Myles Garrett will play his fourth game with the Rams since joining Los Angeles in June.

    Sources indicate that the reigning Defensive Player of the Year missed seven games this season when swelling in his knee dictated in-season surgery. The injury was a major blow after the Rams traded edge rusher Jared Verse alongside their 2027 first-, 2028 second- and 2029 third-round picks to acquire Garrett on June 1. The Rams won the Super Bowl last time it was at their home base, SoFi Stadium. Their all-in actions chased a repeat this season as the game returns to SoFi, and as 38-year-old quarterback Matthew Stafford's career nears its twilight.

    Garrett returned Nov. 8 against the Washington Commanders to the tune of three sacks and six pressures. He registered another pressure in 17 snaps the following week against the Arizona Cardinals.

    Expect Packers quarterback Jordan Love to be his next target.

    It has been revealed that "We played Myles last year, we know what he's about," Love told reporters. "He's a speed guy. He's got power though as well. So he's a great edge rusher, but you got to have a proposal. Obviously we're on the road, so crowd noise will be a little bit of a factor. But you got to be able to be dialed into the snap count and get off on time.

    "Because if you miss a step, Myles is the guy that will be right around you.".

    Garrett and Parsons are not identical players. Each levies a quick get-off to frustrate opposing offensive linemen, but at 6-foot-4 and 272 pounds, Garrett imposes with size beyond Parsons' 6-3, 250-pound frame.

    Each player has flashed against the pass and run. But pass rushing is both players' specialty. One of the NFL's go-to counters for pass rushers of Garrett and Parsons' multi-year All-Pro ilk: establishing the run to keep defenders honest.

    That recipe looks far more promising for one team Wednesday than the other.

    It has been revealed that while the Rams will hurt from the absence of receivers Puka Nacua (season-ending knee surgery) and Davante Adams (hamstring surgery on Oct. 20, with a 6-10 week recovery), Los Angeles has established a diverse offensive attack that also capitalizes on tight ends and running backs.

    Recent findings suggest that in addition to ranking top-10 in passing yards and touchdowns, the Rams rank seventh each in rushing yards and touchdowns. When Parsons chases Stafford, the Rams should have outlets.

    "Anytime you got Matthew Stafford, no matter who's out there in the field, you have a great chance to win," Parsons mentioned. "And they got two incredible backs [in Kyren Williams and Blake Corum], they have a great tight end personnel. I mean, you're seeing a similar variation in Buffalo. They're running a lot of 12P (two tight-end personnel) with Dawson Knox and [Dalton] Kincaid with James Cook out of the backfield. So we're seeing that kind of variation across the league with guys who can fit that personnel set. And [the] Rams [have] been running a lot of 13 personnel [three tight ends]. So it really doesn't surprise me. When you have a great offensive coordinator like that and you can adjust to your system and the players you have, that's why [head coach Sean McVay] is one of the great ones.

    "Regardless of who plays, we got our hands full on Wednesday.".

    The Packers' offense will, too.

    Love deserves credit for how he's carried the Packers this year, his 2,838 passing yards ranking third in the league while his 20 passing touchdowns tie for eighth. He has elevated receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden into a formidable duo who have combined for 12 touchdowns with each accounting for more than 85 receiving yards per game. Green Bay's challenge, as Minnesota exposed in the Packers' last outing: They have no run game.

    Industry observers note that injuries and time on the commissioner's exempt list after allegations of domestic violence have limited running back Josh Jacobs to three games, with Jacobs not expected to return yet this week. Add in a series of injuries to the Packers' offensive line, and the same Green Bay team that ranks third in passing yards (268.1 per game) ranks dead last in rushing yards per game (67) and yards per carry (3.06).

    The result: Opponents know the Packers are overwhelmingly going to pass, and defenses pass-rush accordingly. Love has faced the quickest time to pressure through Week 11, at 2.41 seconds, per Next Gen Stats. He's coming off a game in which the Vikings pressured him on average after 2.33 seconds, the second-fastest mark of his career, generating pressure on 40% of his dropbacks — the most of Love's career.

    Green Bay could receive offensive line reinforcements in center Sean Rhyan and right guard Kevin Zeitler, each of whom is officially questionable per their game status. But will the need to lean on the pass give Garrett and Donald similar confidence to what the Vikings flashed before the Packers' bye?

    Recent findings suggest that "It starts up front," Love noted. "We got to handle business. We got to be able to block the front, give me some time. And in the run game, we got to be able to get hands on people, create some lanes in the run game.

    "You look at their team, the front definitely stands out.".

    If the regular season ended today, the 6-4 Packers would clinch the final NFC wild card while the 6-4 Rams would miss the cut by two spots (the Seattle Seahawks right now slot eighth).

    Those odds will shift after Wednesday.

    The Packers' 40% chance to make the playoffs will improve to 62% if Green Bay wins on Wednesday, per The Athletic's NFL playoff simulator that integrates thousands of possible season outcomes. A loss would drop the Packers' chance to 25%, the major gap in large part due to the tiebreaker that Los Angeles would hold.

    It has been revealed that the Rams have less upside from a win on Wednesday, per The Athletic's predictor, their 34% chance improving to only 47% if they clinch win No. 7. But they have more downside: A loss to the Packers, and the Rams' chance of advancing to the postseason drops to 16%, per The Athletic. Even with a slew of injuries, that would disappoint a club that spent its offseason making a splash for Garrett, acquiring both of the Chiefs' veteran cornerbacks and reuniting with Donald all to upgrade the defense in hopes of maximizing Stafford's waning time.

    It has been revealed that each team is aware of its closing postseason window. And each team is aware that the playoff formula gives no grace on account of injuries — particularly in a crowded NFC.

    "I mean, we're in this conference where it's like you have to play perfect," Parsons remarked. "We don't got the ability [like in] basketball to lose by 40 one night and come win by 30 the next week. That's not in our future.

    "Every game has to be perfect.".

    Will Parsons' return, or Garrett's continued settling into his team, move the needle?

    Restrictions on snap count for Parsons in his first game back would not be surprising. But the Packers have worked him through rehabilitation drills and practices, including with pads, assessing his football skills as well as the symmetry of strength between his quads, hips and calves. Parsons' surgery team led by Dr. Neal ElAttrache also has monitored his post-operation recovery with cameras and force plates that detect strength, speed or functional deficits, ElAttrache told Yahoo Sports by text Tuesday night. The goal with these barometers: Return not only healthy but also with a reduced chance of re-injury.

    Garrett, meanwhile, said he felt rusty in his return vs. the Commanders. Rams head coach Sean McVay qualified that assessment this week.

    Recent findings suggest that "Rusty for him, that's a loose term," McVay said. "I think it's more playing within the system, understanding his opp[ortunities] and understanding who he's rushing with. I think getting the call, applying it, seeing the offense. I think anybody would be rusty. He practiced that whole week [before his return], but before that, he didn't have the accumulation of snaps that a lot of the other guys did or that he would have had if he was healthy the whole time.".

    For both teams, and their ramping-back-up edge rushers, the stakes will echo Wednesday night across the very field each club hopes to revisit in February.

    In a recent development, "Where we're at in the season, like I remarked, every one matters and you don't want to lose games because you're worried about the outcome," Parsons said. "At this point, we can say every game is going to be the difference between playoffs or Cancun.".

    Is a bottom in for the Nasdaq-100? Charts to watch

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
